schema_lineage.changelog: v3.0 scoring scale change: minimum score raised from 0 to 1. Score 0 (No Evidence) is retired. Score 1 now means 'No or Basic Capability' — the floor for any assessed sub-pillar. Score 2 is expanded to a dual definition covering both 'Marketing Mention Only' (vendor claims the capability without technical depth) and 'Basic Manual Capability' (capability exists but is entirely manual with no automation, analytics, or measurable outcomes). Scores 3–5 are structurally unchanged from v2.0. All per-sub-pillar maturity_guidance entries updated to reflect the new 1-5 floor. Coverage grade thresholds retain score >= 2 as the coverage threshold (score 1 = not effectively covered). outcome_maturity_rating scale updated accordingly. Pricing evaluation dimensions retain their structure; outcome_maturity_rating floor raised to 1.
schema_lineage.purpose: Evaluate vendors providing preemptive cybersecurity capabilities — proactive defense architectures that prevent, disrupt, and neutralize threats before exploitation occurs. v3.0 refines the scoring floor to eliminate the ambiguity of score 0 in data pipelines and reporting. Every assessed sub-pillar now carries a minimum score of 1, reflecting that all vendors in scope have at minimum been assessed and found to have no or only a basic presence in that capability area.

preemptive_cybersecurity_taxonomy_v3.0.intent: Assess vendor capability alignment with the preemptive cybersecurity definition. Vendors are evaluated on whether their product delivers capabilities that align with the taxonomy — not solely on AI usage. AI-first and startup markers are retained for market segmentation but are secondary to capability coverage. Most vendors will cover a subset of the 24 sub-pillars; full coverage is rare and not expected. v3.0 uses a 1–5 floor scale where 1 = no or basic capability (assessed but not materially present) and 2 = either a marketing claim or a basic manual implementation. This distinction matters: a vendor scoring 2 may have marketing language about a capability (claim-only) OR a functioning but manual implementation — both represent an early and undifferentiated stage.

metadata.framework_alignment: Gartner Preemptive Security / CTEM Framework + MITRE ATT&CK + NIST CSF 2.0

scoring_scale.note: Score 0 is retired in v3.0. All assessed sub-pillars carry a minimum score of 1. A score of 1 indicates the vendor was assessed and found to have no or only a nominal presence in this capability area. Coverage counts and penetration percentages use score >= 2 as the threshold for 'covered'.

scoring_logic.1: No or Basic Capability: No publicly verifiable evidence of meaningful capability in this sub-pillar. The vendor may be tangentially adjacent to this area but has no identifiable product, feature, or service that materially addresses it. Assessed and confirmed absent or negligible.
scoring_logic.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual: One of two early-stage conditions — (A) Marketing Mention: Vendor marketing or sales materials reference this capability but there are no named products, dedicated features, technical documentation, or measurable outcomes that substantiate the claim. OR (B) Basic Manual Capability: The vendor has a functional capability in this area but it operates entirely through manual analyst effort, manual processes, or professional services engagements with no automation, continuous operation, or scalable delivery. Both conditions represent the same maturity level: the capability is either unsubstantiated or undifferentiated.
scoring_logic.3: Demonstrated: Documented capability with named products or features, some technical detail, and identifiable use cases. Evidence goes beyond marketing claims — there is a real product or service with verifiable functionality. May still lack deep automation or broad customer validation.
scoring_logic.4: Advanced: Named products with measurable outcomes, integration points, customer validation, or analyst recognition. Automation and continuous operation present. The capability is mature, differentiated, and operationally proven.
scoring_logic.5: Market-Leading: Best-in-class capability with deep technical evidence, extensive customer base, analyst leadership recognition, measurable impact metrics, and continuous innovation. Vendor is a recognized leader in this specific capability area.

score_2_disambiguation.description: Score 2 is intentionally dual-definition. Analysts should note which condition applies when scoring.
score_2_disambiguation.condition_A_marketing_mention: Vendor's website, press releases, or sales deck reference the capability by name or implication. No dedicated product page, no datasheet, no technical architecture document, no customer case study, and no analyst mention specific to this capability.
score_2_disambiguation.condition_B_basic_manual: Vendor has a real capability but it is delivered purely through manual analyst work, periodic engagements, or professional services. There is no SaaS platform, no automated scanning, no continuous monitoring, and no scalable delivery mechanism. Client is dependent on vendor headcount rather than technology.
score_2_disambiguation.scoring_note: A vendor with condition A may be scored 2 even without a real product. A vendor with condition B may be scored 2 even with a genuine but manual capability. Both represent pre-differentiated status. The score 2-to-3 threshold is crossed when a named product with technical documentation is verifiable.

source_policy.description: Evidence must be publicly accessible and verifiable.

coverage_grade.description: Letter grade based on percentage of sub-pillars with score >= 2 (24 total in v3.0). Score 1 = assessed but not covered; score 2+ = covered. Grade thresholds are identical to v2.0.

services_maturity_model.description: The Services Capability Maturity pillar captures where vendors sit on the delivery maturity spectrum. This is a progression model aligned to the 1-5 scoring floor — vendors typically advance through these stages as they mature their go-to-market and operational models.

maturity_levels.1_no_service: No meaningful services layer. Technology licensing only with at most basic documentation. No professional services team, no implementation support, no advisory capability.
maturity_levels.2_basic_or_claimed: Either (A) vendor marketing claims a services capability without substantiation, OR (B) vendor provides only rudimentary manual services — basic deployment guides, email support, or occasional consulting engagements with no structured methodology.
maturity_levels.3_managed: Vendor operates the capability on behalf of the client through a structured managed service model. Dedicated analyst teams, 24/7 monitoring, SLA-backed operations.
maturity_levels.4_ai_augmented: Managed services are augmented with AI/ML automation — automated triage, intelligent escalation, ML-driven recommendations. Human analysts focus on high-value decisions.
maturity_levels.5_autonomous: Generative AI and agentic workflows drive autonomous operations. Self-healing, self-tuning systems with minimal human intervention. Represents the frontier of service delivery.

EXM.name: Exposure Management
EXM.focus: Continuous discovery, assessment, and prioritization of exposures across the full attack surface before adversaries can exploit them.
evidence_signals: External and internal asset discovery with real-time inventory
Continuous threat exposure management programs (CTEM)
Risk-based vulnerability prioritization beyond CVSS
Third-party and supply chain exposure monitoring

AMT.name: Automated Moving Target Defense
AMT.focus: Dynamic mutation and randomization of the IT environment to increase attacker uncertainty, cost, and complexity — making static reconnaissance and exploitation unreliable.
evidence_signals: Runtime mutation of memory layouts, network configs, API endpoints
In-process application protection through instrumentation and hardening
Automated network topology reconfiguration and micro-segmentation
Ephemeral credential provisioning and automated key/token rotation

ADR.name: Adversary Disruption
ADR.focus: Active measures to deceive, misdirect, delay, and disrupt adversary operations — increasing attacker cost and exposing threat actor TTPs before damage occurs.
evidence_signals: Decoys, honeypots, honeytokens, and breadcrumbs for high-fidelity detection
Automated threat intelligence ingestion, correlation, and actioning
Proactive hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations
Counter-adversary operations including takedowns and dark web monitoring

PPM.name: Preemptive Posture Management
PPM.focus: Continuous validation, simulation, and hardening of security posture to ensure defenses are effective against real-world attack techniques before incidents occur.
evidence_signals: Breach and attack simulation against production environments
Security control validation (SIEM, EDR, firewall effectiveness testing)
Automated penetration testing and red team exercise capabilities
Cloud security posture management and misconfiguration detection

SVC.name: Services Capability Maturity
SVC.focus: Maturity and completeness of the vendor's services delivery model — spanning implementation, consulting, managed operations, AI-augmented automation, and autonomous service delivery. Evaluates how effectively the vendor wraps technology with operational services that drive client outcomes.
evidence_signals: Professional services for deployment, integration, and onboarding with defined time-to-value targets
Strategic advisory services including CTEM program design, architecture review, and maturity assessments
Managed service operations with 24/7 SOC coverage, dedicated analyst teams, and SLA-backed delivery
AI-augmented and autonomous service delivery using ML recommendation engines, GenAI-powered workflows, and agentic automation

EXM-01.name: Attack Surface Management
EXM-01.expanded_definition: Continuous discovery and inventory of all external and internal assets, shadow IT, cloud resources, and third-party integrations to maintain a real-time map of the exploitable attack surface.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated discovery of internet-facing assets and shadow IT
Real-time asset inventory with risk scoring
Cloud resource discovery across multi-cloud environments
Integration with CMDB and asset management systems
Continuous monitoring for new or changed assets

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor home page or product overview mentions 'attack surface visibility' or 'asset discovery' as a feature area without a dedicated product page or technical documentation.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor offers manual asset inventory or periodic external scanning as a professional services engagement — no continuous automated ASM platform.

EXM-02.name: Continuous Threat Exposure Management
EXM-02.expanded_definition: Operationalized programs that scope, discover, prioritize, validate, and mobilize responses to exposures on a continuous cycle — aligning to the Gartner CTEM framework.
what_to_verify_publicly: CTEM program capabilities or alignment
Exposure scoping and discovery automation
Prioritization based on exploitability and business context
Validation of exposure remediation effectiveness
Continuous cycle operation (not point-in-time)

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'CTEM alignment' or 'continuous exposure management' in a blog post or one-pager without a product that operationalizes the CTEM lifecycle.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor conducts periodic exposure assessments as a consulting engagement — scoped, time-bound, and manual rather than a continuous automated cycle.

EXM-03.name: Vulnerability Prioritization & Management
EXM-03.expanded_definition: Risk-based prioritization of vulnerabilities using exploitability context, threat intelligence, asset criticality, and business impact rather than CVSS alone.
what_to_verify_publicly: Risk-based vulnerability scoring beyond CVSS
Exploitability context from threat intelligence
Asset criticality and business impact weighting
Automated remediation prioritization and tracking
Integration with patch management and ticketing systems

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor mentions 'risk-based vulnerability management' as a differentiator in sales collateral without demonstrating a distinct prioritization engine beyond standard CVSS.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor provides vulnerability prioritization as an analyst-delivered report or spreadsheet — no automated scoring engine or continuous tracking platform.

EXM-04.name: Third-Party & Supply Chain Exposure
EXM-04.expanded_definition: Assessment and monitoring of exposure introduced through third-party vendors, supply chain dependencies, open-source components, and partner integrations.
what_to_verify_publicly: Third-party vendor risk assessment capabilities
Software supply chain monitoring (SBOM analysis)
Open-source component vulnerability tracking
Continuous monitoring of vendor security posture
Supply chain attack detection and alerting

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'supply chain visibility' or 'third-party risk' in a feature list without a dedicated third-party risk or SBOM product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor conducts third-party risk assessments as periodic manual reviews or questionnaire-based engagements — no continuous automated supply chain monitoring.

AMT-01.name: Polymorphic & Morphing Defense
AMT-01.expanded_definition: Runtime mutation of application memory layouts, network configurations, API endpoints, and system identifiers to prevent static targeting by adversaries.
what_to_verify_publicly: Runtime address space or memory layout randomization
API endpoint mutation or obfuscation
Network configuration morphing
System identifier rotation
Evidence of increased attacker cost through dynamic changes

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'moving target defense' or 'dynamic deception' in positioning without a documented AMTD product or technical architecture.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor manually rotates network configs or changes system identifiers as part of periodic hardening engagements — no automated morphing or runtime randomization platform.

AMT-02.name: Runtime Application Protection
AMT-02.expanded_definition: In-process protection that shields applications during execution through instrumentation, code hardening, and real-time exploit prevention without signature dependence.
what_to_verify_publicly: RASP or in-app runtime protection capabilities
Code instrumentation for exploit prevention
Application hardening and anti-tampering
Memory corruption defense (ROP, buffer overflow prevention)
Signature-less exploit detection at runtime

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor mentions 'runtime protection' or 'application hardening' in a feature list alongside EDR or endpoint products without a discrete RASP or instrumentation capability.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor provides application hardening through manual code review or periodic hardening assessments — no continuous in-process runtime agent.

AMT-03.name: Dynamic Network & Infrastructure Defense
AMT-03.expanded_definition: Automated reconfiguration of network topology, micro-segmentation boundaries, and infrastructure parameters to deny adversaries a stable operating environment.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated micro-segmentation with dynamic policy
Network topology reconfiguration capabilities
Software-defined perimeter or zero trust network access
Infrastructure-as-code security automation
Adaptive access controls based on risk signals

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor claims 'zero trust' or 'micro-segmentation' support in marketing but the capability is a basic firewall rule set or network zone — not dynamic or automated.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor implements micro-segmentation through manual policy configuration or periodic network architecture reviews — no automated dynamic reconfiguration.

AMT-04.name: Identity & Credential Rotation
AMT-04.expanded_definition: Automated rotation, obfuscation, and ephemeral provisioning of credentials, tokens, keys, and identity artifacts to limit credential-based attack windows.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated credential and secret rotation
Ephemeral or just-in-time credential provisioning
Service account and API key lifecycle management
Certificate and token rotation automation
Privileged access session isolation

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'credential hygiene' or 'privileged access' in a capabilities overview without a dedicated secrets manager, PAM, or automated rotation product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor provides credential rotation as a manual operational procedure or periodic audit — no automated rotation engine or JIT provisioning platform.

ADR-01.name: Deception Technology
ADR-01.expanded_definition: Deployment of decoys, honeypots, honeytokens, and breadcrumbs across the environment to detect lateral movement, credential theft, and reconnaissance with high-fidelity alerts.
what_to_verify_publicly: Honeypot and honeytoken deployment capabilities
Decoy systems mimicking production assets
Breadcrumb placement for lateral movement detection
High-fidelity alerting with low false-positive rates
Integration with SIEM/SOAR for automated response

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor mentions 'deception' or 'honeypot integration' in a capabilities page without operating a deception platform or offering deception as a distinct product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor manually deploys a handful of honeypots during penetration testing or red team engagements — no persistent automated deception environment.

ADR-02.name: Threat Intelligence Operationalization
ADR-02.expanded_definition: Automated ingestion, correlation, and actioning of tactical and operational threat intelligence to preemptively block, hunt, and disrupt known adversary infrastructure and TTPs.
what_to_verify_publicly: Threat intelligence platform or feed integration
Automated IOC ingestion and correlation
TTP mapping to MITRE ATT&CK framework
Automated blocking based on threat intelligence
Intelligence-driven hunting query generation

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor mentions 'threat intelligence' integration as a feature alongside an EDR or SIEM — no dedicated TIP or operationalization workflow beyond consuming a feed.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor's analysts manually curate and distribute intelligence reports on a periodic cadence — no automated IOC ingestion, SIEM push, or MITRE ATT&CK mapping platform.

ADR-03.name: Proactive Threat Hunting
ADR-03.expanded_definition: Hypothesis-driven and intelligence-led hunting operations that proactively search for adversary presence, persistence mechanisms, and pre-attack indicators before alerts trigger.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed or automated threat hunting services
Hypothesis-driven hunting methodologies
Hunt query libraries and playbooks
Integration with telemetry sources (EDR, NDR, SIEM)
Hunt findings feeding back to detection engineering

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor describes 'proactive hunting' or 'hunt team' in a service overview without differentiated hunt methodology, dedicated hunt analysts, or published hunt playbooks.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor conducts threat hunting as occasional manual exercises by generalist analysts without a structured hypothesis-driven methodology or continuous hunt cycle.

ADR-04.name: Counter-Adversary Operations
ADR-04.expanded_definition: Capabilities to attribute, track, and actively counter adversary campaigns — including takedown services, adversary infrastructure disruption, and dark web monitoring.
what_to_verify_publicly: Dark web monitoring and intelligence gathering
Brand protection and impersonation detection
Takedown service capabilities (domains, phishing, infrastructure)
Adversary attribution and campaign tracking
Digital risk protection services

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'dark web monitoring' or 'brand protection' in a feature list without a distinct digital risk protection platform or takedown service capability.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor performs adversary tracking or dark web research as a manual intelligence service with periodic deliverables — no automated monitoring platform or automated takedown workflow.

PPM-01.name: Breach & Attack Simulation
PPM-01.expanded_definition: Automated simulation of attack chains, lateral movement, and data exfiltration scenarios against production environments to validate detection and prevention control effectiveness.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated attack chain simulation capabilities
Continuous validation against production controls
MITRE ATT&CK technique coverage
Control gap identification and remediation guidance
Reporting on detection and prevention effectiveness

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor mentions 'adversary simulation' or 'purple teaming' as a capability without a dedicated BAS platform or automated control validation product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor conducts manual purple team exercises or scripted attack scenarios on a periodic basis — no continuous automated BAS platform running against production controls.

PPM-02.name: Security Control Validation
PPM-02.expanded_definition: Systematic testing and verification that deployed security controls (SIEM rules, EDR policies, firewall rules, DLP configs) are correctly configured, active, and effective.
what_to_verify_publicly: SIEM detection rule validation and testing
EDR policy effectiveness verification
Firewall and network control validation
DLP and data protection control testing
Configuration drift detection and alerting

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor claims 'control effectiveness' visibility as a feature of a broader platform without a dedicated control validation module or testing workflow.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor validates controls through manual review, configuration audits, or periodic tabletop exercises — no automated continuous control testing capability.

PPM-03.name: Penetration Testing & Red Teaming
PPM-03.expanded_definition: Automated or continuous penetration testing and red team exercise capabilities that identify exploitable paths and validate organizational resilience under realistic adversary conditions.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated penetration testing platform
Continuous or on-demand pen testing capabilities
Attack path analysis and visualization
Exploit validation and proof-of-concept generation
Red team exercise automation (PTaaS)

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor describes 'offensive security' or 'red team services' in a capabilities page without a differentiated automated pen testing platform or PTaaS product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor offers traditional time-boxed penetration testing as a manual consulting engagement — no automated pen testing platform, continuous testing, or PTaaS delivery model.

PPM-04.name: Cloud Security Posture Management
PPM-04.expanded_definition: Continuous assessment of cloud infrastructure configurations, entitlements, and workload security against best practices and compliance frameworks to preemptively close cloud exposure gaps.
what_to_verify_publicly: Cloud misconfiguration detection (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Cloud entitlement and permissions analysis (CIEM)
Compliance framework mapping and reporting
Cloud workload protection capabilities
Infrastructure-as-code security scanning

score_2_examples.marketing_mention: Vendor references 'cloud security' or 'cloud compliance' as part of a broader platform feature list without a dedicated CSPM or CIEM product.
score_2_examples.basic_manual: Vendor performs cloud configuration reviews as periodic audit engagements — no continuous automated CSPM scanning or real-time misconfiguration detection.

EXM-05.name: Exposure Management Services Maturity
EXM-05.expanded_definition: Maturity and delivery model of managed services specifically for exposure management operations — including managed ASM, CTEM-as-a-service, managed vulnerability operations, and outsourced exposure prioritization.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed attack surface management (managed ASM) service offering
CTEM-as-a-service or managed exposure management programs
Managed vulnerability operations with analyst-driven prioritization
Dedicated exposure management analyst teams or SOC coverage
SLA-backed exposure discovery, assessment, and remediation workflows
Continuous managed monitoring of third-party and supply chain exposure

maturity_guidance.1: No exposure management service offering. Technology licensing only. No professional services, no managed ASM, no analyst team for exposure management operations.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor marketing references 'managed vulnerability' or 'exposure management services' without a structured service offering; OR (B) Vendor provides periodic manual vulnerability scans or point-in-time assessment engagements without a continuous managed service.
maturity_guidance.3: Managed ASM or vulnerability operations with dedicated analysts, continuous discovery, and SLA-backed assessments.
maturity_guidance.4: Full managed CTEM program with proactive exposure prioritization, remediation tracking, and continuous analyst-driven operations.
maturity_guidance.5: Autonomous exposure management operations with AI-driven discovery, continuous CTEM orchestration, and self-optimizing remediation workflows.

AMT-05.name: AMTD Services Maturity
AMT-05.expanded_definition: Maturity and delivery model of managed services for automated moving target defense — including managed AMTD deployment, runtime protection-as-a-service, managed micro-segmentation operations, and outsourced credential rotation management.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed AMTD deployment and configuration services
Runtime protection-as-a-service or managed RASP operations
Managed micro-segmentation or zero trust network services
Managed credential rotation and privileged access operations
Continuous tuning and optimization of moving target defense policies
SLA-backed managed services for application hardening or network defense

maturity_guidance.1: No AMTD services offering. Technology licensing only. Client is fully responsible for all deployment, operation, and ongoing management.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor marketing references 'managed AMTD' or 'runtime protection service' without a structured offering; OR (B) Vendor provides deployment documentation and email support with no recurring managed service or dedicated analyst team.
maturity_guidance.3: Managed AMTD or micro-segmentation operations with analyst support, policy tuning, and scheduled reviews.
maturity_guidance.4: Fully managed moving target defense with continuous policy optimization, proactive threat adaptation, and dedicated security engineers.
maturity_guidance.5: Autonomous AMTD operations with AI-driven policy adaptation, self-tuning runtime protection, and continuous zero trust enforcement without manual intervention.

ADR-05.name: Adversary Disruption Services Maturity
ADR-05.expanded_definition: Maturity and delivery model of managed services for adversary disruption operations — including managed deception environments, managed threat hunting, managed threat intelligence operations, and outsourced counter-adversary programs.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed deception-as-a-service with analyst-operated decoy environments
Managed threat hunting services with dedicated hunt teams
Managed threat intelligence operations with analyst-curated intelligence
Managed counter-adversary operations including takedowns and dark web monitoring
Managed digital risk protection services with 24/7 analyst coverage
SLA-backed adversary disruption operations with defined response times

maturity_guidance.1: No adversary disruption services. Technology only. No managed hunting, deception, or counter-adversary service.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'managed threat hunting' or 'deception as a service' in marketing without a defined service with dedicated analysts; OR (B) Vendor provides threat intelligence as periodic manual reports or conducts ad hoc hunting exercises without a structured continuous service.
maturity_guidance.3: Managed threat hunting or managed deception with dedicated analysts, regular hunt cycles, and SLA-backed response.
maturity_guidance.4: Full managed adversary disruption program with continuous hunting, managed deception, intelligence operations, and proactive counter-adversary actions.
maturity_guidance.5: Autonomous adversary disruption operations with AI-driven hunting, self-adapting deception environments, and automated counter-adversary workflows.

PPM-05.name: Posture Management Services Maturity
PPM-05.expanded_definition: Maturity and delivery model of managed services for preemptive posture management — including managed BAS operations, penetration testing as a service (PTaaS), managed security control validation, and outsourced cloud security posture management.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed BAS operations with continuous simulation and analyst-driven gap analysis
Penetration testing as a service (PTaaS) with on-demand or continuous testing
Managed security control validation with analyst-driven effectiveness reporting
Managed CSPM or cloud security posture operations
Dedicated posture management analyst teams with continuous validation cycles
SLA-backed posture management services with defined remediation workflows

maturity_guidance.1: No posture management services. Technology licensing only. No managed BAS, PTaaS, or control validation service.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'PTaaS' or 'managed security validation' in marketing without a defined continuous service; OR (B) Vendor provides periodic manual penetration testing engagements — no continuous BAS, automated simulation, or persistent posture validation service.
maturity_guidance.3: Managed BAS or PTaaS with continuous simulation, analyst-driven gap analysis, and SLA-backed reporting.
maturity_guidance.4: Full managed posture management program with continuous validation, control optimization, and proactive remediation guidance.
maturity_guidance.5: Autonomous posture management operations with AI-driven continuous validation, self-optimizing controls, and automated remediation workflows.

SVC-01.name: Implementation & Onboarding
SVC-01.expanded_definition: Quality and depth of professional services for deploying, configuring, integrating, and operationalizing preemptive security capabilities. Evaluates whether the vendor provides structured onboarding with defined milestones, integration support for existing security stacks, and measurable time-to-value targets.
what_to_verify_publicly: Defined implementation methodology with milestones and timelines
Professional services for integration with existing SIEM, SOAR, EDR, and ticketing systems
Onboarding documentation, runbooks, and knowledge transfer programs
Time-to-value commitments (days to initial detection, weeks to full deployment)
Post-deployment validation and tuning services
API-first integration architecture supporting custom workflows

maturity_guidance.1: No implementation services. Self-serve product documentation only. No professional services team or structured onboarding program.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'professional services' or 'onboarding support' without a structured program with milestones; OR (B) Vendor provides basic deployment guides and email/ticket support with no assigned engineer, no integration playbooks, and no defined time-to-value.
maturity_guidance.3: Structured implementation program with assigned engineer, defined milestones, and integration playbooks.
maturity_guidance.4: White-glove onboarding with custom integration development, validation testing, and defined time-to-value metrics.
maturity_guidance.5: Programmatic onboarding with automated health checks, ML-driven configuration optimization, and guaranteed time-to-value SLAs.

SVC-02.name: Consultative & Advisory Services
SVC-02.expanded_definition: Strategic consulting capabilities that extend beyond product deployment — including security maturity assessments, CTEM program design, architecture review, threat landscape briefings, and ongoing advisory relationships that help clients derive maximum value from preemptive security investments.
what_to_verify_publicly: Security maturity assessment and gap analysis services
CTEM program design and roadmap consulting
Architecture review and security stack optimization advisory
Threat landscape briefings and strategic intelligence services
Executive reporting and board-level security communication support
Ongoing advisory retainer or customer success management with strategic focus

maturity_guidance.1: No advisory services. Product-only engagement. No consulting team, no advisory portfolio.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'advisory services' or 'customer success' in marketing without a structured consulting practice; OR (B) Vendor provides reactive technical support with Q&A responses — no proactive strategic advisory, no structured assessment methodology.
maturity_guidance.3: Formal consulting offerings including maturity assessments or architecture reviews as paid engagements.
maturity_guidance.4: Dedicated customer success with proactive advisory, executive briefings, and program design services.
maturity_guidance.5: Full strategic partner model with embedded advisory, continuous maturity tracking, board-level reporting, and CTEM program co-design.

SVC-03.name: Managed Operations & Continuous Delivery
SVC-03.expanded_definition: Operational capabilities to run preemptive security functions on behalf of the client as a managed service — including 24/7 SOC coverage, dedicated analyst teams, SLA-backed monitoring and response, continuous tuning, and operational governance.
what_to_verify_publicly: 24/7 managed service operations with defined SOC coverage model
Dedicated or named analyst teams assigned to client accounts
SLA-backed detection, response, and reporting commitments
Continuous tuning and optimization of detection rules and policies
Operational dashboards and reporting for client visibility
Escalation procedures, incident management, and governance frameworks

maturity_guidance.1: No managed service offering. Technology-only licensing. Client operates all functions independently.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'managed service' or '24/7 monitoring' in marketing without a structured SOC or dedicated analyst team; OR (B) Vendor offers limited-hours monitoring or basic alert forwarding without full managed operations, dedicated analysts, or SLA commitments.
maturity_guidance.3: Full managed service with 24/7 monitoring, alert triage, and SLA-backed response times.
maturity_guidance.4: Dedicated analyst teams with proactive tuning, operational governance, and continuous improvement cycles.
maturity_guidance.5: Elite managed operations with guaranteed outcomes, continuous posture optimization, and full operational accountability.

SVC-04.name: AI-Driven & Autonomous Delivery
SVC-04.expanded_definition: Use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and generative AI to automate and enhance service delivery — spanning automated triage, intelligent escalation, ML-driven recommendations, GenAI-powered investigation, agentic workflows, and autonomous remediation.
what_to_verify_publicly: AI/ML-powered alert triage, prioritization, and noise reduction in service delivery
Intelligent escalation systems that route to appropriate response tier automatically
GenAI-powered investigation narratives, recommendations, or runbook generation
Agentic AI workflows that autonomously execute response actions with human oversight
Self-tuning detection and policy optimization without manual analyst intervention
Measurable reduction in human analyst effort through AI automation (MTTR, triage volume)

maturity_guidance.1: No AI in service delivery. Fully human-operated manual workflows. No ML, no automation beyond basic scripting.
maturity_guidance.2: Marketing Mention or Basic Manual — (A) Vendor references 'AI-powered' or 'automated response' in marketing without substantiated ML models or autonomous workflows in production; OR (B) Vendor uses basic rule-based SOAR playbooks or scripted automation — no ML models, no AI-generated content, no learning system.
maturity_guidance.3: ML-augmented triage and prioritization. AI recommends but humans decide and execute.
maturity_guidance.4: AI-driven automated response for defined incident classes. GenAI generates investigation narratives and recommendations. Human oversight for critical decisions.
maturity_guidance.5: Autonomous AI-native operations. Agentic workflows self-investigate, self-remediate, and self-optimize. GenAI drives continuous improvement. Human intervention only for novel or high-impact scenarios.

pricing_evaluation.description: Separate evaluation scale assessing the maturity and transparency of the vendor's pricing model for preemptive cybersecurity capabilities. This is NOT a capability assessment — it evaluates how well the vendor's commercial construct serves buyer and provider interests.
pricing_evaluation.framework_source: Gartner Research: 'Pricing Constructs That Support Profitable Business Process Services Revenue' (G00826132, April 2025) and 'Outcome-Based Pricing Fails Tech CEOs in Services' (G00846386, February 2026)

pricing_score_scale.note: Pricing dimensions also use the 1-5 floor scale consistent with v3.0. Score 0 is retired.

scoring_logic.1: No Evidence or Not Applicable: No publicly available pricing information for this dimension. The vendor provides no pricing transparency or this dimension is not applicable to their model.
scoring_logic.2: Marketing Reference or Basic Manual: Either (A) vendor mentions this pricing construct in general terms without specifics; OR (B) vendor has this component but it requires manual negotiation or custom quoting with no transparency.
scoring_logic.3: Documented Structure: Clear description of how this pricing dimension works with published tiers, metrics, or measurement methodology.
scoring_logic.4: Mature and Transparent: Well-defined dimension with real-time tracking, clear measurement, and demonstrated client-facing visibility.
scoring_logic.5: Best-in-Class: Exemplary pricing transparency and composability for this dimension with industry-leading clarity, fairness, and risk-sharing.

PRC-SUB.name: Subscription Transparency
PRC-SUB.definition: Clarity and structure of recurring subscription fees — including breakdown of platform access, agent/sensor licensing, managed service tiers, AI feature add-ons, and support levels.
what_to_evaluate: Published subscription pricing tiers or structure
Component breakdown visible to buyers (platform vs. managed service vs. AI features)
Predictability of recurring costs for client budgeting
Flexibility in subscription scope adjustment (scale up/down)
Transparency about what is included vs. excluded at each tier
PRC-SUB.pricing_model_alignment: Subscriptions provide the revenue floor and budget predictability. Applicable to platform licensing for Exposure Management, AMTD, and Posture Management.

PRC-USG.name: Usage-Based Alignment
PRC-USG.definition: Variable cost components driven by actual consumption — including asset counts, scan volume, simulation frequency, API calls, data ingestion, and compute for AI inference.
what_to_evaluate: Usage-based pricing components clearly defined (per-asset, per-scan, per-simulation)
Measurement systems for quantifying consumption
Real-time usage dashboards or monitoring available to clients
Clear overage policies and escalation thresholds
Alignment of usage fees with computational effort and value delivered
PRC-USG.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to Exposure Management asset-based pricing, BAS simulation frequency pricing, and AI inference charges.

PRC-FIX.name: Fixed Delivery Pricing
PRC-FIX.definition: One-time costs for discrete scope items — including initial deployment, integration setup, deception environment design, pen test engagements, custom playbook creation, and CTEM program implementation.
what_to_evaluate: Clear one-time fees defined for setup and implementation
Scope definition for fixed-fee deliverables
Separation of project costs from ongoing service costs
Change request and scope adjustment processes
Implementation timeline and milestone-based payment structure
PRC-FIX.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to initial deployment of deception environments, AMTD configuration, pen testing engagements, and CTEM program design consulting.

PRC-SUC.name: Success & Outcome Fees
PRC-SUC.definition: Performance-linked pricing components — including bonuses, penalties, or per-unit fees based on achieving engagement objectives, exposure reduction targets, vulnerability remediation rates, or validated control effectiveness metrics.
what_to_evaluate: Defined success metrics tied to pricing
Fees-at-risk component in service agreements
Per-finding or per-validation pricing for pen test and BAS outcomes
Clear measurement methodology and dispute resolution
Balance of risk between provider and client
PRC-SUC.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to BAS and pen testing outcome-based pricing, exposure reduction targets in CTEM services, and control validation effectiveness guarantees.

PRC-COM.name: Composability & Overall Model Maturity
PRC-COM.definition: Overall maturity of the pricing model as a composable, transparent hybrid — assessing whether the vendor's commercial construct can be assembled and reassembled to suit client needs.
what_to_evaluate: Multiple pricing components available and combinable
Client budgeting predictability with spending expectations set upfront
Demonstrated risk-sharing with clear rewards and penalties
Avoidance of excessive variability and dispute potential
Demystification of what the client pays for, when, and why
PRC-COM.pricing_model_alignment: The composable approach is the Gartner-recommended best practice.

PRC-OUT.name: Pricing-to-Outcomes Alignment
PRC-OUT.definition: Assessment of how well the vendor's pricing model is aligned to measurable client outcomes — evaluating whether pricing components are tied to demonstrated security improvements rather than purely input-based metrics.
what_to_evaluate: Pricing components explicitly tied to measurable security outcomes
Outcome-based SLA commitments with financial consequences
Value realization metrics shared with clients
Pricing adjustments based on demonstrated AI efficiency gains
Avoidance of outcome-washing
PRC-OUT.pricing_model_alignment: Gartner research cautions that pure outcome-based pricing frequently fails. This dimension evaluates whether vendors have found a sustainable middle ground.
PRC-OUT.complementarity_note: PRC-OUT may be complementary to other pricing dimensions.

outcome_maturity_rating.description: Overall maturity rating for the vendor's alignment of pricing to security outcomes.
outcome_maturity_rating.framework_source: Derived from Gartner Research: 'Outcome-Based Pricing Fails Tech CEOs in Services' (G00846386, February 2026)

scale.note: Score 0 retired in v3.0. Score 1 = no outcome linkage or no public pricing information.

scoring_logic.1: No Evidence or Input-Only: No public information about outcome linkage, OR pricing is entirely input-based (per-asset, per-agent, per-scan) with no outcome metrics referenced.
scoring_logic.2: Outcome-Aware (Marketing) or Basic Manual: Either (A) vendor references outcomes in marketing but pricing model is not structurally linked; OR (B) vendor discusses outcomes only in custom RFP responses or manual negotiation — no systematic outcome linkage.
scoring_logic.3: Outcome-Linked: Specific pricing components are tied to measurable outcomes. SLAs have financial consequences. Value realization reporting demonstrates pricing-to-outcome correlation.
scoring_logic.4: Outcome-Validated: Pricing model embeds verified outcome metrics with independent or jointly agreed measurement. Client-visible dashboards show real-time outcome performance.
scoring_logic.5: Outcome-Native: The entire commercial model is designed around verifiable outcome delivery with transparent measurement, balanced risk-sharing, AI-efficiency gain pass-through, and continuous value optimization.

evaluation_criteria: Does the vendor's pricing change based on outcomes delivered (not just inputs consumed)?
Are outcome metrics independently verifiable or solely vendor-reported?
Does the vendor share AI-driven efficiency gains with clients through pricing adjustments?
Is outcome alignment embedded in the contract structure or limited to marketing claims?
Does the vendor demonstrate a track record of outcome-based client renewals and expansions?
